decisions.reason: Because the fifteen-day express program is very close to the firm's existing production and service routines, management can learn and refine it with little knowledge stretch, though some overlap with other express offers raises a moderate consolidation risk.

The seventy-two-hour express program still builds on familiar capabilities, but its tighter delivery promise makes execution and margin control harder, so it faces the highest risk of being narrowed or withdrawn if early demand is insufficient.

This fire-resistant steel exterior door fits the firm's established technical, regulatory, and engineering knowledge very well, and the visible launch prominence and approval status suggest strong capacity to improve and commercialize it.

An express delivery program for doors and gates matches the firm's domestic manufacturing, logistics, and service strengths, so absorptive capacity is high and the offer is likely to be retained unless the firm streamlines overlapping express variants.

The online ordering and digital services platform extends the firm's one-stop service model and can be improved through learning from customers and service operations, making it strategically important despite some implementation risk.

A fire and smoke protection door is strongly related to the firm's existing safety-compliance and door-system expertise, so management is likely to keep it and use its in-house R&D and service feedback to enhance it further.
